# Results — Study 669 (RSI-Divergence)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **bullish
price/RSI divergence marks reversals**: price prints a *lower* swing low while RSI(14) prints a
*higher* swing low at the same point, and the textbook says the sellers are exhausted, so price
should turn up shortly after. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints `249b0ef2b1da` (SPY) /
`dd77b24463c4` (QQQ) / `3d13a729a6a7` (IWM) / `1d9e6ffa4dab` (AAPL) / `db3a2e6ab5ea` (MSFT) /
`4f4ce66b8f52` (NVDA).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC, SPY + a five-name liquid basket (QQQ, IWM, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA), each **4,147 rows**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30 |
| Pattern definition | swing low = strict minimum of a centred **11-bar** (`order=5`) window; **confirmed** `order`=5 trading days after it prints (that is how a swing low is *defined* — you cannot know it was the low until you have seen the following bars, exactly as a chartist would draw it); bullish divergence = a confirmed swing low with a *lower* price than the previous confirmed swing low but a *higher* RSI(14) reading |
| Events | **109 confirmed bullish divergences** across 6 tickers, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30 (AAPL 16, IWM 16, MSFT 22, NVDA 22, QQQ 15, SPY 18) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the signal-vs-unconditional split; **Newey-West (lag = h)** *t* on the pooled dummy regression as the overlap-robust cross-check (h-day forward windows overlap); Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 200-draw random-signal placebo (matched signal count per ticker) |
| Execution / costs | one documented execution lag: enter at the **next session's open** after confirmation (zero look-ahead — everything used to confirm the pattern is public by that close); exit at the close h sessions later; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow (this is a bullish pattern) |
| Data quirks (named) | no survivorship: SPY/QQQ/IWM are index ETFs, AAPL/MSFT/NVDA are still-listed mega-caps — this basket cannot manufacture a fake edge from delisted losers, but it also skews toward a strong 2010-2026 bull market, so the *unconditional* hit rate (not 50%) is the fair "coin" |

## The headline — divergence-signal forward return vs the unconditional baseline

| horizon | signal mean | unconditional mean | gap | Welch *t* | NW *t* (lag=h) | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d  | +1.89 bps (n=109) | +31.60 bps (n=24,743) | **−29.71 bps** | **−0.62** | −0.63 | 52.3% (Wilson [43.0%, 61.4%]) |
| 10d | +57.58 bps (n=109) | +68.83 bps (n=24,713) | **−11.25 bps** | **−0.20** | −0.20 | 56.0% (Wilson [46.6%, 64.9%]) |
| 20d | +84.08 bps (n=109) | +145.26 bps (n=24,653) | **−61.17 bps** | **−0.84** | −0.82 | 56.9% (Wilson [47.5%, 65.8%]) |

At every horizon the divergence-flagged trades earn **less** than an unconditional day on the
same six tickers, not more — the gap is negative all three ways, and no *t* comes anywhere near
the ±2 bar (the largest magnitude is 0.84). The pattern doesn't clear the desk bar in either
direction; if anything the point estimate is a laggard, not a leading indicator.

## Random-signal placebo — does the pattern beat a same-sized random signal?

20 seeds × 200 draws (4,000 draws total) of the same **number** of random dates per ticker as
the real divergence count, right-tail test (p = share of random draws whose mean **≥** the
observed divergence mean — the claim predicts a positive edge):

| horizon | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p(random ≥ observed) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d  | +1.89 bps  | +32.19 bps (36.12) | **0.799** |
| 10d | +57.58 bps | +71.01 bps (50.38) | **0.613** |
| 20d | +84.08 bps | +150.53 bps (71.43) | **0.827** |

This is the honest teardown of the folklore: a **random** signal of the identical size, on the
identical tickers, beats the actual RSI-divergence signal on 61-83% of draws. The pattern isn't
just "no better than random" — most random alternatives outperform it.

## Era contrast — pre vs post the zero-commission retail era (split 2019-10-01, justified: Schwab/Robinhood cut equity commissions to zero in Oct 2019, and retail chart-pattern trading — RSI divergence is a textbook retail setup — went frictionless and crowded)

| era | signal mean (h=10d) | n | Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010 → 2019-10 | +20.16 bps | 68 | |
| 2019-10 → 2026 | +119.64 bps | 41 | **+0.83** |

The point estimate is larger in the recent slice, but the difference is **not certified**
(*t* = +0.83) — there is no decay *or* crowding story to tell here; both eras are statistically
indistinguishable from each other, and both are already indistinguishable from noise on their
own.

## Third axis — a timer with costs (h=10d hold, the headline horizon)

| cost (one-way) | gross | net |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5 bps  | +57.58 bps/trade | **+47.58 bps/trade** |
| 10 bps | +57.58 bps/trade | **+37.58 bps/trade** |

Hit rate **56.0%** (Wilson [46.6%, 64.9%]) — worst trade **−14.3%**, best trade **+18.1%**. For
reference, the **unconditional** hit rate on this same basket at the same 10-day horizon is
**59.7%** (n=24,822): the six-ticker basket has such a strong embedded drift that "beating a
coin" is the wrong bar. Divergence trades hit their target **less** often than doing nothing.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic random walk with periodic engineered dips (so genuine swing lows recur); a
TUNABLE bounce is planted exactly on the dates the study's **own detector** flags as a confirmed
bullish divergence (never a hand-tuned proxy for it); no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bounce = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.31** (sd 1.08), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted bounce = +2.0% over 5 bars (seed 669) | **+6.96** (n=102 events) |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up hard on a planted post-signal bounce. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Divergence-flagged forward returns are **negative relative to the
  unconditional baseline at every horizon tested** (−29.7 / −11.3 / −61.2 bps at 5/10/20d,
  Welch *t* −0.62 / −0.20 / −0.84, NW cross-check matches), and a random signal of the identical
  size beats the real pattern on 61-83% of placebo draws. No sign of a reversal edge in either
  magnitude or hit rate (52-57% vs a 59.7% unconditional bar).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even before costs the gross edge is at best a coin flip against the
  basket's own drift; 5-10 bps of one-way cost strips real money from an already-negative
  edge, and the worst single trade (−14.3%) dwarfs the average win.
- **"Beats a random signal?" — BUSTED.** The random-signal placebo — the fairest possible
  control, matched ticker-by-ticker on signal count — outperforms the real RSI-divergence
  pattern on the clear majority of draws at every horizon (p = 0.61-0.83). The textbook picture
  (exhausted sellers, a higher RSI low presaging a bounce) does not survive contact with 16
  years of daily data on six liquid US tickers.
